facts.site: Yandarra Downs Open Cut and Heavy Workshop
facts.title: fire on SG-9000 during routine operation

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was medical treatment injury, with 1 person injured.

defences.finding: Control EARTH_LEAKAGE_PROTECTION: the earth leakage and protection setting integrity was in place but did not perform, and the accident investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.

Control HAZARDOUS_AREA_EQUIPMENT_INTEGRITY: the integrity of explosion-protected equipment in zoned areas was never verified as effective, and the accident investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.
Control SWITCHING_AUTHORISATION: the authorisation of switching and access to apparatus had been bypassed, and the accident investigation classified this as an individual or team action.
Control ZERO_ENERGY_VERIFICATION: the proving zero energy before intrusive work was not in place, and the accident investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the earth leakage and protection setting integrity on SG-9000 and TX-9001 and record the spot check before this task is next authorised.
Restore the integrity of explosion-protected equipment in zoned areas on SG-9000 and TX-9001 and record the spot check before this task is next authorised.
Restore the proving zero energy before intrusive work on SG-9000 and TX-9001 and record the spot check before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in controlling access to energised apparatus, specifically working live under a documented justification. SG-9000 (mine switchgear) is in service for pit and workshop distribution. The task proceeded during routine operation while the earth leakage and protection setting integrity was in place but did not perform. The electrical energy involved is held as HV switchgear, and the recorded presentation was shock, arc flash, unplanned energisation.
response.summary: On 2 April 2009 an incident occurred on SG-9000 and TX-9001 at Yandarra Downs Open Cut and Heavy Workshop during routine operation, releasing electrical energy held as HV switchgear.
